source: FLEURS dev transcripts, through bournemouth_aligner's std G2P
note: Tone is a separate layer, not part of these tokens: see the tone guide. Affricates and diphthongs are split into tokens: 在 = t s a ɪ, 这 = ʈ ʂ ɤ; an aspirated affricate puts the aspiration on its second half (其 = t ɕʰ i, 此 = t sʰ i). Give each part its own span. The aspirated stops pʰ tʰ kʰ are the sounds written p t k in pinyin and Jyutping; the plain p t k are the ones written b d g.

SIL.name: silence
SIL.plain: A pause: no speech. Use it for a pause the speaker makes inside a segment.

noise.name: noise
noise.plain: A non-speech sound: a breath, cough, laugh or click.

<unk>.name: unknown
<unk>.plain: The G2P wrote a sound this model has no token for. Keep its time span; the label cannot say what it is.

a.name: open front unrounded vowel
examples: k w ɔ k k a

i.name: close front unrounded vowel
examples: s ɐ i k a i

e.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel
e.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”
examples: f e i s œ ŋ

l.name: alveolar lateral approximant
examples: l ɐ ŋ l ɪ k

o.name: close-mid back rounded vowel
o.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”

m.name: bilabial nasal
examples: t ʊ ŋ m ɐ t

f.name: voiceless labiodental fricative
examples: f e i s œ ŋ

ə.name: mid central vowel (schwa)
examples: ɛ <unk> ə n s tʰ ɑ l

p.name: voiceless bilabial stop
examples: p ɐ t tʰ ʊ ŋ

w.name: labial-velar approximant
examples: k w ɔ k k a

ɑ.name: open back unrounded vowel
examples: ɛ <unk> ə n s tʰ ɑ l

ŋ.name: velar nasal
examples: j ɪ ŋ h œ ŋ

ʊ.name: near-close back rounded vowel
examples: p ɐ t tʰ ʊ ŋ

h.name: voiceless glottal fricative
examples: <unk> ɑ k h <unk> m p t ə n

ʂ.name: voiceless retroflex fricative
ʂ.plain: a hard sh with the tongue tip back (Polish “sz”)

y.name: close front rounded vowel
y.plain: ee said with rounded lips (French “tu”, German “über”)

ɕ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative
ɕ.plain: a soft sh, with the tongue body raised (Polish “ś”)
examples: t ɕ ɪ n ɕ ɪ ŋ

ɵ.name: close-mid central rounded vowel
ɵ.plain: a rounded vowel between e and o (Swedish short u)

œ.name: open-mid front rounded vowel
œ.plain: e as in “bed” said with rounded lips (French “neuf”, German “können”)
examples: f e i s œ ŋ
x w a ɕ ɥ œ

ʈ.name: voiceless retroflex stop
ʈ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”)

tʰ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, aspirated
tʰ.plain: t as in “ten”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: p ɐ t tʰ ʊ ŋ

kʰ.name: voiceless velar stop, aspirated
kʰ.plain: k as in “key”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

sʰ.name: voiceless alveolar fricative, aspirated
sʰ.plain: s; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: j ɐ n t sʰ i

pʰ.name: voiceless bilabial stop, aspirated
pʰ.plain: p as in “pen”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: pʰ o u pʰ i n

ɥ.name: labial-palatal approximant
examples: x w a ɕ ɥ œ

ɕʰ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative, aspirated
ɕʰ.plain: a soft sh, with the tongue body raised (Polish “ś”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ʂʰ.name: voiceless retroflex fricative, aspirated
ʂʰ.plain: a hard sh with the tongue tip back (Polish “sz”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɚ.name: r-coloured schwa
ɚ.plain: a weak vowel with an r colour (American “butter”, Mandarin “er”)

ɻ.name: retroflex approximant
ɻ.plain: an English-like r with the tongue tip curled back

m̩.name: bilabial nasal, syllabic
m̩.plain: m; syllabic: forms a syllable with no vowel, as the n of “button”. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language
